subject: FRE
label: Grade 08
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 08 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Past and future in simple form
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Past and future in simple form', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: talk about past and future. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Past and future in simple form' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: talk about past and future, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Model run for 'Past and future in simple form'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Talk about past and future: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.

rubric: Explains the idea to someone else
Practises most days and keeps evidence
checks: Unit 1 (Past and future in simple form): show that you can talk about past and future. What are the first and last step you used?

Any correct example is fine. A good answer names the first step (see or say the idea) and the last step (check or reflect) from the model run, and meets the standard: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
Unit 2 (Daily routine): show that you can describe a day. What are the first and last step you used?

Any correct example is fine. A good answer names the first step (see or say the idea) and the last step (check or reflect) from the model run, and meets the standard: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
Unit 3 (Listening practice): show that you can follow a longer dialogue. What are the first and last step you used?

Any correct example is fine. A good answer names the first step (see or say the idea) and the last step (check or reflect) from the model run, and meets the standard: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
Unit 4 (Speaking practice): show that you can present. What are the first and last step you used?

Any correct example is fine. A good answer names the first step (see or say the idea) and the last step (check or reflect) from the model run, and meets the standard: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Past and future in simple form), and at which Bloom level is it?
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Speaking practice) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
